email.subject: Order arrived damaged - tea gift box
email.body: Hi, I ordered a tea gift box from your Beijing Chaoyang store last week and it arrived today. The outer box was fine but when I opened it, the gift box inside was crushed on one corner and a couple of the tea tins were dented. This was supposed to be a gift for a friend's birthday this weekend, so I'm pretty disappointed. I already called the store earlier and the person I spoke to said to email with photos, so I've attached a few. I'd really like to get this sorted before Saturday if possible. Thanks.

pending_progress.instruction: Describe the supported pending request once. Do not assert acceptance OR non-acceptance without evidence.

evidence_intake.order_reference: Ask for missing order reference or purchase proof only for the actual unresolved verification; never for praise/thanks relay.
evidence_intake.photos: Use attachment_evidence source states. Ask conditionally for useful missing evidence; never ask again for reported sent files.
evidence_intake.permission: Customer may reply with relevant details; no guaranteed visit availability.

knowledge.advice: Offer a proportionate apology. Keep packaging and existing photos; ask to share photos merely taken, check receipt if reported sent. For damaged electrical equipment do not power on before qualified assessment. Ask for missing order proof only. Check repair/replacement and logistics handling, do not establish cause or guarantee entitlement.
Preserve the exact deadline. The pending task should check replacement stock, expedited delivery and alternatives; no guaranteed arrival.

service_brief.permitted_closing: Thank customer; wish pleasant use where appropriate. Invite customer to provide missing information or ask for progress. Do not commit staff to future contact.
service_brief.attitude: Apologize proportionately for actual harm even with neutral expression; thank praise; no unsolicited warnings about resolved faults.
